Rules changed since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the case's seven rules only "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function" changed, and it is graded against the current text. The other six are graded to the 2026-10-23 standard: a passing --check-formatted after a file's last edit counts as formatted for Before you finish step 1; a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU is clean under the return-tuple rule when its @doc says so; a case for a single fallible call is not exercised under the with rule; Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside or before %{cart | items: ...} is not the forbidden pattern; a code kept as a string and checked against a literal list is clean under the atom rule.

Chain fallible steps with `with`, per run, against the new text. haiku-1 writes no with and no case on a fallible call (it checks membership with if normalized in @codes, lines 61-65): not exercised. haiku-2 writes no with; its one fallible call is a single-step case with a pass-through clause, lines 60-63 `case parse_code(normalized) do` / `{:ok, discount} -> {:ok, %{cart | discount: discount}}` / `{:error, :unknown_code} = error -> error` / `end`: not exercised, per the instruction for this batch. The body cannot fail and there is no else, so the new text would allow `with {:ok, discount} <- parse_code(normalized), do: ...` here; note that the rule's second example block now shows this exact case shape as its Instead of, so a strict grader could read it as a violation, and the next rewording should say whether the pass-through case is forbidden or only not preferred. sonnet-1 writes two one-step withs, apply_code/2 lines 83-85 and total/2 lines 107-109, neither with an else, and neither body can fail (line 84 builds a tuple; line 108 adds the results of apply_discount/2 and shipping_fee/1, which return integers): clean, decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`." sonnet-2 writes one one-step with, apply_code/2 lines 72-74, with no else and a body that builds a tuple: clean by the same sentence. No run wrote a one-step with that has an else or a fallible call in its body, so the 'any other one-step with is a case' half and the second-<- sentence were not exercised. Under the old text ("A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`.") sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 would both be violated, as the Sonnet runs in the last three sweeps were for the same shape, so the rewording moves this case from 2 of 4 to 0 of 4 by allowing the shape, not by a change in the code.

Other rules, graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Atoms: haiku-2 (lines 91-93), sonnet-1 (112-114) and sonnet-2 (97-99) use one parse_code/1 clause per code string, haiku-2 after trimming and upcasing; haiku-1 keeps the trimmed, upcased string and checks it against @codes ~w(SAVE10 FREESHIP) (lines 10, 61). defstruct: [:items, :code] in haiku-1, [:items, :discount] in the other three, all bare atoms. Money: integer div in all four, rounding halves up. Naming: domain names throughout, no boolean, get, fetch, size or length functions.

The other rewordings of this round are outside the case's rule list (the index rows for the `do:` rule, the pipeline rule, the capture rule, the named-argument rule, the Enum table, Read configuration at runtime and the ExUnit grouping rule do not name shop-project), and no run breaks any of them: no do: body holds a fn, a capture with arguments, or a case; no pipeline sits on one line in lib, tests or doctests; no capture other than the project's own &(&1 + quantity); no multi-line literal passed inline and no literal of more than six elements; no List.keyfind/3 or filtering for; every module attribute is a literal (@shipping_fee 499, @codes ~w(SAVE10 FREESHIP), @prices %{...} in two test files); every describe is named after one function. The new `->` clause rule is also outside the list and no run breaks it: every one-line case clause is under 70 characters, and the longer remove_item/3 clauses are broken. sonnet-2's lines 77-79 put a one-expression body, {:error, :code_already_applied}, in a block where `do:` would fit in 95 columns; as in the 2026-10-22-b grades, a one-expression body written as a block is not counted, since no sentence of the do: rule says it is wrong, although its new first sentence names a tuple as a do: body.
